name: delivery-instructions
title: Delivery instructions
description: Where the courier should leave it: hand over, door, neighbour or locker, with the safe choice first and only the fields that choice needs.
docs: A fieldset that is controlled with value and onChange or keeps its own state from defaultValue; the value is { dropOff, neighbour, code, phone, note, saveAsDefault }. options (value, title, description, icon, flag, fields) are the cards, safest first: description is the line about the risk the choice carries, flag is a short word such as 'Safest', and fields lists which of 'neighbour', 'code', 'phone' and 'note' that choice needs. Only those fields are shown, in place, and a polite status names the choice and the fields that appeared. The layout answers to the width of the fieldset, not of the screen: the cards sit one above the other until there is room for two, so it also works in a drawer or beside a sidebar on a wide screen. The code and the phone number share a row, and whichever of them is asked for alone takes the whole row. The access or gate code is masked with a button to show it, the note is a textarea with a counter against noteLimit (default 200) and showPhone={false} leaves out the phone number for the courier. Under 'Save as my default for future orders' a line says in words whether the instructions apply to this order only or to the next ones too. locale joins the list that is read out after a choice and labels holds every word.
